data.title: Chile's pension funds requested curbs on interest-rate bets before losses, Bloomberg reports
data.description:
Executives at Chile's pension funds appealed to regulators for curbs on volatile interest-rate derivatives before a downturn in US Treasuries left them with billions of dollars in losses, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday.

The report said that fund managers had flagged risks of positions that have since hit the system's most conservative fund hard. The losses have drawn criticism from some lawmakers and raised concerns among pensioners.

Chile's private pension system is managed by firms known as Administradoras de Fondos de Pensiones (AFPs), or pension fund administrators, which oversee five investment funds ranging from Fund A, the riskiest, to Fund E, the most conservative.

Earlier this week, the AFP Association's head of research, Roberto Fuentes Silva, attributed a decline in Fund E to rising US interest rates after Bloomberg reported that Chilean pension funds had posted losses of about $7.7 billion on interest-rate-related positions.

Executives managing these pension funds had asked regulators in private conversations to enforce rules on the stockpiling of volatile derivatives, Bloomberg's Thursday report said, citing people familiar with the conversations.

The lucrative nature of the trade meant the executives could not act independently without forgoing returns that rivals would continue to cash in, the report added.

Chile's pension regulator did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment.

The AFP Association has sought to reassure contributors, saying in a statement that pension fund performance should be assessed over the long term rather than based on short-term market fluctuations.

"A pension fund does not have losses or gains; rather, it experiences increases or decreases in its valuation," Fuentes Silva told local media.

Chile's current private pension system started in the early 1980s during the Augusto Pinochet dictatorship and relied solely on worker contributions managed by the AFPs.

The system has long faced criticism for generating relatively low pensions while AFP operators continue to post significant profits. After years of political debate, Congress approved a major pension reform in January 2025, with the rollout beginning in stages from August last year and continuing over several years.

data.title: DOCOMO and Abside Networks Sign Memorandum of Understanding on HAPS
data.description:
TOKYO, JAPAN and BOSTON, USA, Oct 16, 2026 - (JCN Newswire) - NTT DOCOMO, INC. and Abside Networks, Inc. signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) on October 13, 2026, toward the development of future communications infrastructure utilizing high-altitude platform stations (HAPS*1) and realizing of next-generation networks leveraging artificial intelligence (AI). Going forward, the two companies will conduct joint studies toward future collaboration in areas including wide-area, high-capacity and massive-connectivity communications using HAPS, network control and data utilization.

Background

DOCOMO has been conducting studies and demonstrations toward the realization of wide-area communications services utilizing HAPS. To deliver high-quality communications services via HAPS, it is important to develop radio access networks (RANs) and communications equipment suited to the stratospheric environment. As conditions in the stratosphere differ from those on the ground, communications equipment and network design must be adapted accordingly, requiring specialized knowledge and experience.

Abside has many years of experience in stratospheric communications. Through Project Loon*2, Abside developed knowledge and experience in stratospheric communications and has been engaged in the development of HAPS communications equipment and RAN technologies. Abside is also developing non-terrestrial network (Non-Terrestrial Network, NTN) technologies and AI-based network control technologies.

As a result, the two companies confirmed that their respective visions and technologies may be complementary and signed the MOU to jointly explore potential future collaboration toward networks that integrate the ground, stratosphere and space.

Scope

Under the Initiative, the two companies will jointly study technical collaboration for the future use of HAPS. The principal areas of study are as follows:

- System architectures for wide-area, high-capacity and massive-connectivity communications using HAPS

- Application of AI to demand forecasting and the control of beams, capacity, spectrum and interference in stratospheric RANs

- Collection and utilization of data relating to communications quality, network operations and sensing in the stratosphere

- Future integration with external applications and service platforms

Future Outlook

DOCOMO is independently studying a future network vision based on a three-dimensional communications infrastructure that integrates AI with NTN initiatives, including HAPS. The vision aims to address growing communications demand accompanying the expanding use of AI by realizing wide-area, high-capacity communications and advanced network control using NTNs, including the stratosphere, in addition to terrestrial networks. Its realization will require RAN and network orchestration technologies capable of integrated control across terrestrial networks (Terrestrial Network, TN) and NTNs.

Abside is developing radio equipment for TN and NTN RANs that uses a large number of antenna elements (Very Large Array) to enable high-spatial-resolution and precise beam control Abside is also developing an AI-driven software platform that provides integrated control of networks across the ground, stratosphere and space.

Going forward, the two companies will bring together their respective expertise and technologies and pursue joint studies toward the realization of next-generation communications infrastructure utilizing HAPS and AI.

*1 Unmanned aerial platforms that operate in the stratosphere at an altitude of approximately 20 kilometers. By equipping the platforms with wireless communications equipment, HAPS is being studied as a means of providing coverage in areas that have traditionally been difficult to serve, including airspace and maritime regions, as well as underserved locations such as sparsely populated and mountainous regions where conventional coverage has not been economically viable.

*2 A stratospheric communications project led by Google that sought to provide communications services using high-altitude balloons. For more information, please visit: https://x.company/projects/loon/

*3 AI 3D Networks, AI3DN(TM), is a vision central to 6G deployments of a single AI-driven network spanning terrestrial, stratospheric and space-based layers, built on the high-spatial-resolution foundation of Abside's AI3DR(TM) RAN product lines. For more information, please visit: https://www.abside-networks.com/AI3DN/

This release is part of "NTT C89," a space-business brand promoted by NTT Group companies. "NTT C89" is a trademark of NTT, Inc, and is an abbreviation of "NTT CONSTELLATION 89 PROJECT." The initiative aims to contribute to the expansion of space-related businesses and the overall development of the space industry through the delivery of solutions to society. For mor information, please visit: https://group.ntt/jp/aerospace

About Abside Networks

Abside Networks is a telecommunications equipment manufacturer headquartered in Massachusetts, United States. In addition to wireless equipment for mobile network operators, the company develops private wireless systems for enterprises, government agencies and defense applications. Abside offers AI3DR(TM), its AI Ready RAN and Radio product lines for terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks, providing the high-spatial-resolution foundation required by AI 3D Networks (AI3DN*3), a vision central to 6G deployments.

About NTT DOCOMO

NTT DOCOMO, Japan's leading mobile operator with over 93 million subscribers, is one of the global leaders in 3G, 4G and 5G mobile network technologies. Under the slogan "Bridging Worlds for Wonder & Happiness," DOCOMO is actively collaborating with global partners to expand its business scope from mobile services to comprehensive solutions, aiming to deliver unsurpassed value and drive innovation in technology and communications, ultimately to support positive change and advancement in global society. https://www.docomo.ne.jp/english/

data.title: Super Micro Stock Has 45% Upside, Says Rosenblatt -- Here's the Bullish Case
data.description:
Super Micro Computer's challenge is turning a large AI server order pipeline into profitable growth while rebuilding investor confidence in its financial management. Rosenblatt Securities maintained its $51 price target.

Analyst Sajal Dogra retained a Buy rating. His target compares with a reference share price of $35.09, suggesting potential upside of about 45.5%. The valuation uses roughly 10 times his fiscal 2027 earnings-per-share estimate.

Demand provides the growth case. Super Micro has more than $60 billion in AI server orders from over 20 customers. Dogra expects Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform to reach higher-volume deployment by the January quarter, potentially supporting additional server demand.

Profitability remains a key test. Rosenblatt forecasts a gross margin of 11% in fiscal 2027, making cost control important as the company works to fulfill orders.

The appointment of CFO Mark Long adds another factor. At Western Digital (WDC), his previous employer, Long helped reduce debt principal by about $2 billion in fiscal 2018 and lower borrowing costs. Dogra views the leadership change, improved internal controls and clean fiscal 2026 audit as steps that could ease governance concerns. Wall Street's consensus rating remains Hold, with an average price target of $39.38.

data.title: Cantor Calls WULF, HUT, CORZ Stocks ‘Generational Buys’ Amid Price Target Cuts Across The Sector
data.description:
Key points:
  • Cantor Fitzgerald flagged rising interest rates and capitalization-rate pressures as key headwinds for AI infrastructure valuations.
  • It added that potential capital expenditure overruns and project execution risks are adding to investor concerns about the sector.
  • Despite cutting its price targets, Cantor maintained ‘Overweight’ ratings on all seven stocks.

Shares of Bitcoin (BTC) miners that have expanded into AI and high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure extended their declines in morning trade on Friday, with the group on track for a mostly losing week amid a broader rotation out of technology and AI-related stocks.

Cantor Fitzgerald analyst Brett Knoblauch added to the pressure by lowering price targets on seven AI data center stocks. However, he kept ‘Overweight’ ratings on all of them.

In a note to investors cited by TheFly, he said the group had sold off broadly since its June highs. He called TeraWulf (WULF), Hut 8 (HUT) and Core Scientific (CORZ) a “generational buy” that could rally 100% or more once AI funding fears ease.

HUT stock fell over 4% in morning trade, while CORZ and WULF shares dropped around 1% each. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for both CORZ and WULF improved to ‘bullish’ from ‘neutral’ over the past day. Sentiment around HUT remained in the ‘bullish’ zone.

Why Are AI Infrastructure Stocks Falling?

According to Cantor, rising interest rates and capitalization-rate pressures, potential capital expenditure overruns, execution risks, political uncertainty and growing opposition to data centers are weighing on the sector.

It added that investors are also increasingly concerned about the capital intensity of AI infrastructure projects and the visibility of catalysts that could support further gains.

Cipher Mining Gets The Biggest Price Target Cut 

Cipher Mining (CIFR) saw the steepest reduction, with Cantor cutting its target by a third, to $19 from $28, followed by CleanSpark (CLSK) and Core Scientific. CIFR stock and CLSK shares fell over 3.5% each in morning trade.

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around CIFR rose to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bullish’ territory over the past day, while sentiment around CLSK moved to ‘bullish’ from the ‘neutral’ zone.

The Funding Backdrop

The sector’s pullback has coincided with mounting concerns over the cost of funding AI infrastructure projects. CoreWeave (CRWV) shares dropped over 7.5% in morning trade on Friday, as yields on its bonds climbed above 15%.

The yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury also briefly rose above 5.3% earlier this week, adding pressure to capital-intensive businesses.

Prior to Cantor’s repricing, Morgan Stanley also cut price targets on several Bitcoin miners expanding into AI infrastructure last week, citing “evolving” credit-market conditions. However, it raised its price targets on Hut 8 to $275 from $273 and TeraWulf to $65 from $62.50, leaving both well above Cantor’s revised outlook.

data.title: Erasca Terminates Chief Operating Officer Chetwyn in Streamlining
data.description:
By Colin Kellaher

Erasca is parting ways with its chief operating officer, Nicholas Chetwyn, in a streamlining of the clinical-stage precision oncology company's reporting structure.

Erasca on Friday said in a Securities and Exchange Commission filing thatother members of the San Diego company's leadership team will assume Chetwyn's duties as it realigns responsibilities to support the development and potential commercialization of its RAS-targeting programs.

Chetwyn, who joined Erasca in March 2021 and has been chief operating officer since May 2023, will depart effective Nov. 2, the company said.

data.title: US FDA sets up board to oversee drug exclusivity determinations
data.description:
The US FDA's drug evaluation department said on Friday it has formed a board to oversee and advise on exclusivity determinations made by the department, aiming to improve clarity and consistency of those decisions.

Here are more details:

  • FDA-granted exclusivity rewards innovation by giving newly approved drugs a period of market protection, before lower-cost generic competitors enter the market

  • The CDER (Center for Drug Evaluation and Research) exclusivity board will oversee certain exclusivity determinations, including whether and what type of exclusivity should be granted and the appropriate scope of grants, the agency said on Friday

  • The board will focus on 5-year new chemical entity exclusivity that is granted to a drug whose active ingredient has never before been approved by the FDA

  • It will also oversee 3-year new clinical trial exclusivity grants that are meant for drugs that use a previously approved active ingredient, but their approval relies on new clinical studies conducted or funded by the sponsor

  • It will advise on exclusivity for biological products too

  • The board will not review other types of exclusivity apart from the three, it said

  • The board also may evaluate and make recommendations regarding CDER's policies and practices relating to exclusivity and maintain records of exclusivity determinations

data.title: Asian gasoline margin slides as Chinese barrels return
data.description:
By Mohi Narayan

Asian gasoline margins nearly halved on Friday from a record high hit at the beginning of the month, as Chinese refiners resumed fuel exports, easing immediate supply concerns, traders and analysts said.

The refining profit, or crack, (GL92-SIN-CRK) for gasoline plummeted to about $24 per barrel over Brent crude from a record peak of $50.53 on October 1. However, the margin remains well above $13 a barrel recorded in October last year.

"Supply situation has improved at the prompt at least, as Chinese exports have returned," Stuti Jhunjhunwala, oil market analyst at Energy Aspects said.

"Also, refining runs in Asia, excluding China, are likely to increase in the fourth quarter, contributing to supplies", she added.

Gasoline cracks typically weaken during the winter months in the northern hemisphere due to lower demand, but a tight supply outlook due to a war in the Middle East, a Russian export ban and a few unplanned outages at regional refineries at a time when inventories were lower at key trading hubs drove margins to a record.

Restocking at key inventories like Singapore also helped ease supply concerns, even though Middle East shipments remained constrained, analysts said.

"Singapore light distillate inventories rose for a second consecutive week to a one-month high, pointing to improving product availability in Asia," LSEG Research said in a note.

Light distillate inventories, including naphtha and gasoline, rose to a one-month high of 13.806 million barrels in the week to October 14, Enterprise Singapore data showed on Thursday.

Gasoline imports into the major trading and blending hub rose about 11% to 320,000 tons or the equivalent of 2.7 million barrels during the period, while exports were down about 23% on the week at roughly 486,000 tons.

Gasoline inflows were led by China at nearly 177,000 tons, followed by Brunei at about 64,000 tons. Outbound volumes were led by Indonesia at about 221,000 tons, followed by Malaysia at around 105,000 tons.

The price for benchmark-grade fuel also eased to $129.20 per barrel on Friday from a near seven-month high of $150.69 per barrel touched on October 1; however, they were also seasonally at a higher level. (GL92-SIN)

data.title: U.S. Industrial Production Faces Headwinds — Market Talk
data.description:
1109 ET - A solid rise in U.S. industrial production in September still leaves some lukewarm indicators. Production rises 0.7% in the month. Citi's Veronica Clark and Andrew Hollenhorst say in a note that "manufacturing production has moved mostly sideways since the spring and remains below production levels of 2014-18." They add that manufacturing production rose "a more modest" 0.3%. "While strong AI-demand has boosted business investment, much of this investment is imported, implying domestic production has not been as strong," Clark and Hollenhorst say. They add that higher interest rates and fading fiscal support represent headwinds to non-AI manufacturing into 2027. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)

1033 ET - Unlike in recent years, the British economy has sustained its early-year momentum into the second half of 2026, Oxford Economics' Andrew Goodwin says in a note. "This likely reflects a combination of genuine strength due to structural change because of IT-related investment, but also noisy data," he says. Rapid increases in AI usage mean recent IT strength will likely endure, though strong pickup in professional services output in the last six months is harder to explain. Any resilience will come under pressure over the next few quarters, particularly given most of the impact of the Middle East war is still to come. Financial conditions have worsened, and fiscal policy is being tightened, he adds. (edward.frankl@wsj.com)

1026 ET - If Albertans and Quebecois did vote to leave Canada, what would that mean for the rest of the country? Capital Economics' Bradley Saunders argues the blow to GDP from losing Quebec industry and Alberta oil and gas could be mediated somewhat by continued free trade, companies relocating from seceding provinces to the rest of Canada and a weaker Canadian dollar boosting export competitiveness in other sectors. As such, the economist expects the rest of Canada to outperform the two provinces, whose newfound independence would likely require fiscal tightening. Of course secession would be a lengthy and complicated process without precedent and as such there remains a lot of uncertainty, Saunders says. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)

1026 ET - Canada's housing market remains soft, with a combination of higher fixed mortgage rates and potential Bank of Canada tightening likely keeping buyers on the defensive, Bank of Montreal's Robert Kavcic says. The economist continues to argue that market pricing of a percentage point in interest rates increases in 2027 is too aggressive, but says the balance of risk is tilting to the upside for variable rates into the coming spring market for housing. "This poses an issue for the market given that variable rates are currently the lowest available by a relatively wide margin, and most buyers have pivoted to that space," he says. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)

1024 ET - Elevated oil prices boosted Canada's purchasing power but the gains are uneven across the country, Royal Bank of Canada says. Real gross domestic income expanded 3.1% on-year in 2Q, nearly triple the pace of real GDP growth after a 46% surge in oil added about C$12 billion a quarter to export revenue. Royal Bank says oil producers and resource-rich provinces are capturing a disproportionate share of the initial windfall, while most households face higher costs without offsetting income gains. This complicates monetary policy, since the Bank of Canada controls only one interest rate for the entire country, Royal Bank adds. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)

1018 ET - The rise in mortgage rates has sent Canada's housing market into reverse, with sales and prices both falling in September, says Capital Economics' Stephen Brown. With the risk mortgage rate rise further prices could fall a bit more in the coming months, though Brown doesn't anticipate the Bank of Canada will lift its policy rate as aggressively as markets are pricing in. Lenders have been forced to pass on higher funding costs to fixed mortgage rates. Yet while home prices may fall near term, Brown says he is more upbeat about the outlook from mid-2027 as mortgage rates drop back next year. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)

1011 ET - The widening of spreads between French and German government bond yields has had as much, or possibly more, negative impact on the euro as widening Treasury-German spreads, Standard Chartered's Steve Englander says in a note. "Rising French credit default swaps (CDS) also have a significant impact on euro; although the relationship is not as tight as with the French-German spread, the CDS correlation still supports the view of concerns about France's government finances." The euro faces renewed depreciation if spreads widen further, he says. The euro rises 0.3% to $1.1256 after hitting a 17-month low of $1.1112 Wednesday, LSEG data show. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

0929 ET - The impact of the October 28 U.K. budget on sterling depends on the implications for economic growth and debt sustainability, Ebury's Matthew Ryan says in a note. A positive case for sterling would be restoring the fiscal headroom to around 15-20 billion pounds and modest spending increases with small, targeted take hikes and early revenue. "Less long-dated issuance would likely ease pressure on 30-year U.K. government bonds and provide the pound with modest upside." This would provide room for the Bank of England to raise interest rates in November, he says. A negative scenario would be a fiscal headroom of less than 15 billion pounds with bigger spending increases and back-loaded tax hikes with uncertain revenue, he says. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

0911 ET - The euro might struggle to sustain current gains against the dollar as French fiscal risks persist, Monex Europe analysts say in a note. The 10-year French-German government bond yield spread is off its early-October highs but there are ongoing tensions over the government's proposals to reduce the budget deficit. With the European Central Bank likely to keep rates unchanged on October 29, the euro is beholden to French developments and the dollar, they say. Monex sees $1.11 as the "key downside marker" for the euro and thinks gains will prove limited while French fiscal uncertainty and the Gulf conflict persist. The euro rises 0.2% to $1.1242 after earlier reaching a 10-day high of $1.1269, according to LSEG.(renae.dyer@wsj.com)

0907 ET - Treasury yields edge higher but are on pace to end the week with a decline as markets increasingly price in an interest rate hold by the Fed this month. Chairman Warsh stops short of giving forward guidance, as officials head to the blackout period preceding the FOMC meeting. Inflation remains a concern in financial markets, but the risk of economic slowdown due to steep borrowing costs keeps a lid on yields. U.S. import prices rise more than expected in September. The 10-year yield is at 5.115%, compared to 5.086% yesterday and 5.243% a week ago. The two-year is at 4.768%, up from 4.747% yesterday and down from 4.789% last week. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.co; @ptrevisani)

0808 ET - The dollar's falls could prove short-lived given the prospect of further tightening by the Federal Reserve, Trade Nation's David Morrison says in a note. The dollar is weaker as investors seem convinced the Fed will leave rates unchanged on October 28 after some policymakers recently signalled no rush to raise rates further, he says.However, once November's midterms are over, the Fed could be forced to raise rates "rather aggressively" if inflation continues to rise. The DXY dollar index trades within a band of support between 101.20 and 101.50, and if it can hold above here, it could resume rising, he says. The DXY falls 0.4% to 101.674 after earlier reaching a two-week low of 101.576.(renae.dyer@wsj.com)

0649 ET - The euro has received a boost from this week's unease over U.S. artificial intelligence stocks and could be entering a decent consolidative phase after recent losses, ING's Chris Turner says in a note. The euro could rise to $1.1340-$1.1350, he says. "But do not expect euro-dollar to be the big outperformer on a further U.S. equity correction." A lower dollar versus the Swiss franc would likely take the lead in this case, he says. The euro rises 0.4% to a one-week high of $1.1263, having reached a 17-month low of $1.1112 Wednesday, LSEG data show. The dollar falls to a two-week low of 0.8228 francs. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

data.title: Hedge fund Two Sigma ends real estate unit fundraising, cuts staff - report
data.description:
Quantitative hedge fund Two Sigma Investments has halted efforts to raise $2B for its real estate investment unit and cut senior staff, as rising interest rates hobbled its fundraising efforts, according to a media report on Friday.

The unit's partner and chief investment officer, Rich Gomel, is leaving the company. Others on the real estate leadership team, including two of the three remaining partners and one of the two heads of data science, are also departing, Bloomberg News reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

The firm, which had targeted raising ~$2B for the business, pulled in less than half that amount, some of the people told Bloomberg. Some of the real estate team will remain to manage its existing portfolio of properties.

Rising interest rates have weighed on commercial property valuations and led to owners holding assets for longer. Bloomberg, citing data from PEI Group, noted that private real estate fundraising totaled just over $30B for Q3 2026, the lowest quarterly total since early 2013.

Two Sigma started forming the real estate business in 2019 and launched it with internal capital about two years later. It was led by former Blackstone Vice Chair Tom Hill, who left the firm last year, one of the people told Bloomberg.

The business started taking outside capital in 2024 with its Real Estate Opportunity Fund, which mostly focused on housing and industrial investments, with some selective stakes in hospitality and office real estate. The hedge fund's strategy was to use the firm's data to power predictive tools that could project supply and demand, which would determine investment decisions.

data.title: Nvidia and Mercedes-Benz Extend AI Driving Deal
data.description:
Mercedes-Benz (MBGAF) and Nvidia are expanding their work on automated vehicles, with the latest phase bringing together onboard computing, AI-driven driving decisions and additional safety protections as they pursue more advanced driving capabilities.

A key objective is to prepare for SAE Level 4 applications, in which vehicles can operate autonomously within defined conditions. The companies identified robolimousines as a potential application, but did not provide a timetable for deployment.

The development will draw on several technologies. Mercedes-Benz's MB.OS supports vehicle functions and remote software updates, while Nvidia's Hyperion provides the computing and sensor framework. Nvidia's Alpamayo Stack is designed to help vehicles interpret driving situations and make decisions using AI reasoning.

The partnership also incorporates Nvidia Halos, which adds a separate safety layer intended to provide backup protections. Planned capabilities include navigating urban routes between destinations, automated parking and active safety functions.

For Mercedes-Benz, the extended collaboration could help bring more driving features into its software platform. Nvidia gains a continued role in the automaker's automated-driving development. Neither company provided additional commercial terms or a launch schedule in the supplied announcement.

data.title: Euro zone bonds steady after safe-haven rally, French debt set for best week since August
data.description:
Key points:
  • Money markets fully price chance of ECB rate rise in December
  • French 10-year yield premium over Bunds narrows to about 138 bps
  • IMF expects one more ECB rate hike this year

By Amanda Cooper

Euro zone government bond yields steadied on Friday but were still set for a weekly decline, thanks to bonds' recent safe-haven rally sparked by concern about AI-related companies' ability to deliver a return on their vast spending.

Global bonds are heading for their strongest weekly performance in four months, with yields on the sovereign debt of G7 economies down by an average of 8.7 basis points to 4.273%, according to LSEG data.

The shares and bonds of more indebted companies linked to the artificial intelligence build out were hit hard earlier this week, which weighed on the broader equity market and pushed investors back into bonds.

Yields on German 10-year Bunds (DE10YT=RR), the safe haven of choice for many investors in European assets, have fallen nearly 7 bps this week to around 3.42% on Friday, though were up 1 bp on the day. Two-year yields (DE2YT=RR) were 2 bps lower on Friday at 3.06%.

"Concerns about the AI boom are making government bonds look like better value," said analysts at Societe Generale.

However, "we have been here before" they cautioned, saying they doubted this was the end of the AI investment frenzy and the end of the cycle.

Government debt, which traditionally acts as a shock absorber for ructions in riskier assets, has been unable to perform this function for most of this year, as the surge in energy and food prices as a result of the Middle East war has forced investors to price in the prospect of higher borrowing costs in the form of higher yields.

The correlation between Bunds and the STOXX 600 , for example, has turned positive — meaning yields are more likely to fall when stocks fall and vice versa — this week for the first time since early August.

This relationship reached its most negative on record in late September, according to LSEG data.

As well as the impact of the war in the Gulf, central bankers from the world's largest economies gathering in Bangkok said the AI boom was also creating fresh inflation pressures and financial risks, because the investment is arriving long before the productivity gains AI promises.

FRENCH DEBT STABILISES

One of the major aggravating factors for bonds has been the persistent concern among investors about the long-term finances of developed-market governments.

Yields on French bonds (FR10YT=RR), which have been among the most harshly punished in the past few weeks, given the deep-rooted worry about France's ability to tackle its finances, were trading around 4.79%, flat on the day, and down 7 bps this week, set for their largest weekly drop since early August.

The premium of French 10-year yields over Bunds (DE10FR10=RR), a reflection of the extra compensation investors want for the risk of lending to France, rather than Germany, was around 137 bps on Friday, having fallen from a 15-year high of nearly 160 bps on October 2.

"We remain defensive on (French) OATs given the fiscal and political risks," said Soc Gen.

"Beware of new waves of volatility as the budget debate is ongoing and investors are not keen to add a lot of risk."

Money markets show traders do not believe the ECB will raise interest rates at its meeting this month, but upped the chances of a December rate hike to 100%, from just below that level earlier in the day. At least one more hike is priced in by next April (0#EURIRPR).

There was little reaction to data that showed harmonised inflation in the euro zone ran at a five-year high of 3.8% in September, in line with expectations in a Reuters poll of economists.

The IMF said in its regular forecast for Europe it expects one more ECB rate hike this year.

  • Morgan Stanley lowered its price target to $195 from $200 and maintained an ‘Underweight’ rating.
  • JB Hunt’s revenue reached $3.68 billion, exceeding Fiscal AI’s $3.58 billion estimate, while net earnings edged up to $172.4 million from $170.8 million a year earlier.

JB Hunt (JBHT) shares drew investor attention on Friday after several analysts lowered their price targets following the company’s third-quarter earnings, as higher operating costs and margin pressure tempered its strong revenue growth.

According to The Fly, Wells Fargo lowered its price target to $285 from $305 and maintained an ‘Overweight’ rating. The firm said the third-quarter cost trend was as expected, while the intermodal pricing outlook was better despite slower volume.

Morgan Stanley lowered its price target on the stock to $195 from $200 and maintained an ‘Underweight’ rating. According to The Fly, analyst Ravi Shanker said the third quarter laid bare cost pressures flagged at the Laguna conference a month earlier, adding that a recovery through pricing would take time and effort.

Meanwhile, JPMorgan lowered its target to $283 from $287 while maintaining an ‘Overweight’ rating. The firm said the wide discount to truckload is still pulling through record conversion activity, but “most investors continue to overestimate how quickly JBI margins can improve.”

JB Hunt’s Q3 Earnings Highlights

J.B. Hunt reported third-quarter revenue of $3.68 billion, up 20% year over year, beating the $3.58 billion estimate compiled by Fiscal AI. Net earnings edged up to $172.4 million from $170.8 million a year earlier.

The company reported diluted earnings per share (EPS) of $1.82, up from $1.76 a year earlier, compared with analysts’ estimate of $1.80, according to Fiscal AI. However, operating income increased 2% to $247.1 million, while operating margin narrowed to 6.7% from 7.9% a year earlier.

Dedicated Contract Services operating income fell 22% to $81.7 million, driven by higher driver personnel expenses, group medical claims, insurance premiums, equipment costs and new-business onboarding expenses. Final Mile Services operating income declined 76% to $1.6 million, primarily due to lower revenue and higher purchased transportation expenses.

How Retail Views JBHT

Retail sentiment surrounding JBHT on Stocktwits remained in ‘Neutral’ territory over the past 24 hours, amid ‘High’ message volumes.

JBHT shares have gained over 18% year-to-date.

data.title: U.S. Industrial Production Faces Headwinds — Market Talk
data.description: A solid rise in U.S. industrial production in September still leaves some lukewarm indicators. Production rises 0.7% in the month. Citi's Veronica Clark and Andrew Hollenhorst say in a note that "manufacturing production has moved mostly sideways since the spring and remains below production levels of 2014-18." They add that manufacturing production rose "a more modest" 0.3%. "While strong AI-demand has boosted business investment, much of this investment is imported, implying domestic production has not been as strong," Clark and Hollenhorst say. They add that higher interest rates and fading fiscal support represent headwinds to non-AI manufacturing into 2027. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)
